newsitem.title: UK: House of Fraser may need more surgery.
newsitem.headline: House of Fraser may need more surgery.

text.p: British department store chain House of Fraser probably needs more radical surgery to improve its performance, but cost-cutting plans announced on Monday were along the right lines, retail analysts said on Monday.
"It is at such a low level some improvement is certain, but it depends on how much and how sustainable it is," said one retail analyst.

The group earlier announced plans to sell three of its 51 stores, cut around 1,000 jobs and clear unwanted stock. It estimated it would need provisions of between 41 million and 49 million stg to cover the restructuring. Analysts are forecasting pretax profits for the current year of about 14 to 15 million stg, excluding exceptionals.
Analysts agreed the firm probably had more to do to reduce costs. "I don't think this is necessarily the end of the story," said another retail analyst.
Last October the company said it could close between five and 10 of its stores in wide ranging review of its business.
John Richards, retail analyst at NatWest Markets, said he believed the group's performance would improve.
"The new management team is starting to do some of the basic things right," he said. NatWest recommends buying the shares at current levels.
The stock was up 0.5 pence at 142.5 by 1451 GMT. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
